detailed_description: The Text to ASCII Art tool turns short text into a five-line ASCII banner in the browser. Enter up to 20 characters, choose the fill character from block, #, *, @, $, or +, and click Convert. The page uses one built-in standard ASCII font and displays the result in a monospace output box. Use Copy to place the generated banner on your clipboard for a README, terminal message, note, or small decorative text block.
usage_steps: Type or paste short text into the input field.
Choose the character used to draw the banner.
Click Convert to generate the ASCII art.
Click Copy to copy the result to your clipboard.
usage_examples: Create a short banner for a README or command-line welcome message.
Make a retro heading for notes about terminal tools.
Generate a simple decorative divider for documentation.
Compare how the same word looks with block, hash, star, at, dollar, or plus characters.

faqs.question: How long can the input be?
faqs.answer: The input field allows up to 20 characters so the banner stays readable in the output area.

faqs.question: Can I choose the drawing character?
Can I copy the output?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Copy after generating the ASCII art.

faqs.question: Where is the conversion performed?
faqs.answer: The conversion runs in the browser using the built-in character map.
